🚨🇲🇽 <u>Harfuch: no foreign forces operate on Mexican soil</u>

As Washington floats "military options" against the cartels, Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch drew the line: "It's not about whether we want it — our law does not allow foreign forces in our country." Cooperation means shared intelligence, not US agents running operations here; the capture of "El Mencho," he noted, was carried out 100% by the Mexican Army.
banner: MEXICO: NO FOREIGN AGENTS ON OUR SOIL

🇲🇽🐄 <u>US reopens its border to Mexican cattle after 14 months</u>

After 14 months sealed over a screwworm outbreak, the US reopened its border to live Mexican cattle today, starting at Agua Prieta, Sonora. The fix wasn't a wall — it was science: a sterile-fly plant in Chiapas, co-financed by both governments, that SADER is now scaling up to wipe out the pest. More than a year of Mexican-led coordination reopened a market Washington shut unilaterally.

<u>LA TIMES</u>: Did Mexico create a "blacklist" of journalists and politicians?
August 21, 2026 | 🟡

A presidency official projected a slide of critical journalists and opposition figures at the morning press conference. LA Times put the opposition's "enemy list" charge in the headline — then, to its credit, quoted Sheinbaum flatly denying any intent to censor.

Left out of the frame: the slide ran in the government's official "right of reply" segment rebutting specific coverage — not a secret dossier, a distinction the word "blacklist" erases.

• Sheinbaum, in 2021, on the same idea: "Who makes lists? McCarthyism, Nazism, fascism."

<u>AP</u>: 2,300 Mexicans deported to Guatemala and Honduras
August 21, 2026 | 🔴

The US is now shipping Mexican citizens to third countries — nearly 2,300 to Guatemala, dozens to Honduras — then busing them to southern Mexico so they can't cross back. Mexico objected. Washington did it anyway.

Until this year Mexicans were deported almost exclusively home; the shift began in April. Mexico has separately protested 17 of its nationals dead in US custody or during enforcement.

• DHS: "the largest deportation operation in history, just as President Trump promised"
• civil groups call it a way "to increase pressure on Mexico"

<u>RAW STORY</u>: US deported its own cartel witness — three times
August 23, 2026 | 🤡

The DOJ built cases on his testimony against Mexican cartels. Then ICE deported him — three times — including to Mexico, where a judge had ruled he'd "more likely than not" be tortured. A federal judge just ordered him brought back.

Rubio and ICE's acting director personally terminated his torture protection days before removal; Guatemala refused him, Mexico declined him, and he was dumped on Aug 1 without his phone.

• "put himself at enormous risk to turn on the cartels and testify against them"
• "target for a hideous death if they ever got their hands on him"
banner: US Deported Its Own Cartel Witness 3x

🇲🇽💰 <u>MEXICO'S INFLATION HOLDS NEAR 3.26% — STILL AMONG ITS LOWEST IN YEARS</u>

Mexico's annual inflation ran 3.26% in the first half of August, El Economista reports — still parked near five-year lows and within reach of Banxico's 3% target, with services the only real pressure while Banxico holds its rate at 6.50%. A strong peso and anchored prices: as Washington lectures the world on "stability," Mexico just keeps posting it.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO AND PERU RESTORE TIES — AND SHEINBAUM STILL STANDS WITH CASTILLO</u>

Mexico and Peru have restored diplomatic relations, nine months after Lima cut them over Mexico granting asylum to Betssy Chávez, ex-premier to jailed president Pedro Castillo. A Mexican Air Force jet flew Chávez to safety under the 1954 Caracas Convention, and Sheinbaum didn't blink: "we will continue in defense of President Castillo… fraternity is the seal of our peoples." Mexico's asylum tradition, from the Spanish Republic to today, isn't for sale.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>21ST-CENTURY FASCISM IS TARGETING MEXICO'S 4T, WARNS CONTRALÍNEA</u>

A Contralínea analysis warns that 21st-century fascism — advancing through genocide while waving the flag of "democracy" — now weaponizes elections, media and "free speech" against Latin America's progressive governments, Mexico's Fourth Transformation among the targets. Political scientist Pablo Rojas Gómez notes the left still hasn't built a unified answer to a US-backed reaction that no longer needs tanks to topple a government.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO PULLS RECORD $40.8B IN FOREIGN INVESTMENT — BUT ITS OWN BOSSES WON'T SPEND</u>

Mexico attracted a record 40.871 billion dollars in foreign direct investment in 2025, yet Contralínea notes only 7.377 billion was genuinely new money — the rest was reinvested profits and intercompany loans. Total investment sits at 21.2% of GDP against China's 41%, and R&D is a meager 0.20%. The 4T state builds the trains, ports and social wage; the national bourgeoisie pockets nearshoring and cries "uncertainty" instead of investing.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>THREE OF EVERY TEN ONLINE PROPERTY LISTINGS IN MEXICO ARE FAKE</u>

Three of every ten real-estate ads on Mexican websites are fraudulent, La Jornada reports, and with 7 of 10 property deals now starting online, the internet has become a hunting ground. Scammers clone legitimate agency pages, phish personal data through links and QR codes, and post homes that don't exist — a wave that took off in early 2024 as housing search moved to the screen.
